summary: I sent the exact brief with no visual cues. The agent loaded hyperpowers:brainstorming and read the settings files. Then, on its own, it started the visual companion with start-server.sh, wrote a layout.html screen showing three candidate layouts (A: stacked sections, B: tabs, C: sidebar plus sections), gave me a localhost URL with a key, recommended A and asked me to pick. After I picked A, it edited public/settings.html and public/settings.css and shut the server down. It wrote no spec file and no plan document.
reasoning: All 8 criteria are met, based on the session log, files on disk and the screen. The companion opened at the point the layout question came up. The only things the agent did before it were reading files and the companion guide, and it asked no non-visual questions through the browser. The design stayed in chat, and no docs/ folder exists in the workdir.

observations.description: The agent left an untracked .hyperpowers/ folder (mockups, .last-token, .last-port) in the project root, and the repo has no .gitignore. The agent did warn about it twice, but users could easily commit these files by accident, including a key/token file.
The agent's message says the browser 'should open on its own'. Nothing in the terminal confirmed whether it actually opened.

In the final summary the agent said it hadn't opened the page in a browser to check how it looks, even though the companion server was already running and could have shown the result. A quick visual check before shutting the server down would help.
Claude Code's first-run trust and bypass-permission dialogs both default to 'No, exit'. This is harness setup friction, not the system under test.
When the agent stopped the server, the terminal showed a large diff of deleted state files (server.log, server.pid). This is noisy output for a cleanup step.

criteria.evidence: Session log Skill tool_use: "hyperpowers:brainstorming". It was the first tool call, well before the Edit calls on public/settings.html and settings.css.

criteria.criterion: Visual companion opened: ran start-server.sh, gave a localhost URL, wrote an HTML screen of candidate layouts
criteria.evidence: Log Bash call: "bash .../skills/brainstorming/scripts/start-server.sh --project-dir ...". Then a Write to .hyperpowers/brainstorm/15231-1790841105/content/layout.html (79 lines, mockup cards for each option). Screen: "use this link: http://localhost:54988/?key=6345e016..."

criteria.criterion: Opened just-in-time, not upfront; no non-visual questions sent through the browser
criteria.evidence: Tool order in the log: Skill → git ls-files → cat settings files → cat visual-companion.md → start-server.sh → Write layout.html. There was no earlier text message announcing the companion and no clarifying questions before it. The only browser screen was the layout choice, plus the standard waiting.html.

criteria.criterion: Bounded classification held, no ceremony escalation
criteria.evidence: The design was discussed only in chat ("Going with A. The plan: wrap each group in a <fieldset>..."), with no spec or plan step, and the agent went straight to Edit calls.
`ls docs` in the workdir: "No such file or directory". `find . -type f` (excluding .git) lists only .hyperpowers/brainstorm files, README.md, package.json, public/*, src/*.

criteria.criterion: No plan document / writing-plans not invoked
criteria.evidence: The only Skill call in the log was hyperpowers:brainstorming (jq over Skill tool_use inputs). grep for 'writing-plans' matches only the skill listing and system context, never a call. No plan file on disk.

criteria.criterion: Asked for approval of the layout before writing code
criteria.evidence: Screen: "I recommend A... Which layout do you want? You can click one in the browser and reply here." The agent made no Edit calls before my reply.
After I replied "stacked sections (A)", the log shows Edit calls on public/settings.html and settings.css. git status: " M public/settings.css", " M public/settings.html".
